main: Governance at Thirdway is the framework by which the business is led, monitored and held to account. It applies to how the company is structured, how decisions are made, how performance is measured, and how the interests of clients and other stakeholders are protected across every project.
Thirdway's leadership is structured across four tiers:
Managing Directors, each accountable for their own P&L
Non-Executive Directors, providing independent oversight of the Board
Performance is reported monthly at each level of the business. The full executive team meets quarterly to review performance, strategy and risk across the group.

The Board is currently composed of 38% women and 62% men, with tenure ranging from under five years to over ten. This composition reflects a mix of long-standing directors and more recently appointed members.

Thirdway's board composition sits within a broader national context of improving gender balance in UK corporate leadership. According to the FTSE Women Leaders Review 2026, women now hold 43% of board seats across the FTSE 350, up from 9.5% when the review began in 2011. Thirdway continues to monitor its own board composition against this benchmark as part of its ongoing governance review.
Thirdway's Board includes two Non-Executive Directors,
,  who provide independent challenge and oversight separate from the executive leadership team.

Thirdway operates a defined set of controls and procedures to safeguard the interests of clients and other stakeholders across each project. These controls are structured around the project lifecycle, covering:

This framework is designed to support collaboration between internal teams and external partners, with the aim of maintaining consistent standards of productivity, quality and value across all projects.

Thirdway has implemented a structured approach to contracting, designed to standardise and streamline the contracting process across its projects. The stated aims of this approach are more efficient project operation, clearer oversight for all parties, and more effective co-operation between Thirdway and its clients during delivery.
Thirdway's in-house legal team was shortlisted and "Highly Commended" in the
, in recognition of this approach to contracting.
Thirdway tracks a defined set of business metrics as part of its governance and reporting process:

Reporting on these metrics is limited to information considered decision-critical, in order to support timely and independent decision-making by business leaders. This is supported by the company's approach to regulatory compliance, and by ongoing investment in people and product development.

Senior Leadership, which comprises Thirdway's technical directors, is responsible for setting and maintaining performance standards across the business, and reports against these standards on a regular basis.
Tenure across Senior Leadership is mixed: a number of directors have held their roles for over a decade, while others have joined more recently.
Thirdway maintains the following governance mechanisms:
Formal evaluations are conducted twice a year, combining self-assessment with board feedback.
Professional experience, qualifications and tenure are tracked across the leadership team.
Directors are required to disclose any conflicts of interest as they arise.
A dedicated committee oversees ESG matters, supported by an Executive Director for Sustainability.
The Board receives regular reports on leadership pipelines, skills, inclusion and retention, along with metrics on hiring times, turnover and demographic shifts.
